thread:
jia: Heads-up from support: customers saw dropped hedged requests when policy routed to alternate region. appears policy wasn't reducing weight when the runtime signaled degraded capacity.
oliver: Do we have traces? was it because runtime cb opened or because node-level CPU contention?
mira: Trace snippet from request 8f3a:
```
2026-02-03T11:02:10Z request=start route=us-east-1->us-west-2 policy_choice=hedge_count=2
2026-02-03T11:02:10Z runtime(us-west-2): health=degraded cb_until=1675559000 load_est=0.9
2026-02-03T11:02:11Z runtime(us-west-2): request=rejected reason=queue_full
```
jia: Policy saw stale health=ok metric from 30s earlier and still hedged to us-west-2.
infra-bot: :robot_face: note: we currently only expose aggregated health via telemetry every 45s. per-request headers are only available in sidecar mode.
oliver: Root cause: decision horizons mismatch + telemetry staleness. We need a lightweight, per-request runtime hint that policy can trust without sidecar RPC.
mira: Proposal: add small header map from runtime in the LB layer: X-Runtime-Hint: "cb_s=12;cap_frac=0.35;ts=1700000000". Policy will parse and immediately mark variants with cap_frac < 0.5 as low-weight for hedging for the next cap_frac_ttl (use cb_s as min).
jia: Also want to encode a "degrade_penalty" float so runtime can express expected tail inflation on that node (e.g., +0.3 p99). That prevents policy from picking quantized fallbacks if they increase tail.
oliver: Agree. That keeps policy simple: score' = base - alpha*latency - beta*cost - gamma*degrade_penalty. Add a hard rule: if cb_s > probe_interval, skip probe.
infra-bot: :warning: security note: header must be signed for Private deployments to prevent tenant spoofing. add HMAC header X-Runtime-Hint-Sig.
qa-jen: How do we avoid timestamp spoofing/clock skew? If runtime ts differs from policy time, TTLs break.
mira: We'll use server-side monotonic acceptance: policy will only accept hints where abs(now - ts) < 2m. If hint ts too old, treat as stale and log metric policy.hint.stale. If ts too far ahead, reject and alert.
jia: Edge case: proxies may strip custom headers. LB must be configured to forward X-Runtime-Hint for internal traffic only. we'll gate header on internal network path.
oliver: Implementation option A: have LB inject hint at egress of runtime process so it's always present on response path. Option B: runtime sidecar attaches hint, but we need to avoid extra RTT. A seems better.
mira: Scoring config example (pseudo):
```
policy:
  hedging:
    default_hedge_count: 2
    min_cap_frac: 0.5
  scoring:
    weights:
      latency: 1.0
      cost: 0.8
      degrade_penalty: 1.5
    hard_rules:
      skip_if_cb_s_gt_probe_interval: true
```

jia: Observability: emit policy.hint.applied and policy.hint.ignored with tags {route,variant,reason}. Also record hint.sig.validation_failures.
qa-jen: Testing plan: unit tests for parser, e2e with LB-injected header in staging, and chaos run where runtime toggles cb to ensure backoff prevents probe storms.
oliver: Timeline: Mira can PR LB header + schema this week. Policy changes (parser + scoring tweak + stale acceptance) next week. Ops: enable header in staging in Canary mode for three days before wider rollout.
mira: One more safety: add per-variant probe-budget counter in policy persisted to memcache so restarts don't reset probe backoff. cap budget at 3 probes per 10m per-variant.
jia: Action items:
- LB: inject X-Runtime-Hint with ts, cb_s, cap_frac, degrade_penalty; include X-Runtime-Hint-Sig (mira)
- Policy: parse header, enforce ts skew, apply hard skip rules, factor degrade_penalty into score, persist probe-budget (oliver)
- Infra/Security: define signing secret rotation + HMAC verification (infra-bot)
- QA: add e2e tests and chaos scenario (qa-jen)

mira: I'll open the RFC with header schema and scoring example. pls comment.
jia: Thanks, team. If rollout goes well we'll remove the 45s telemetry reliance and get much faster convergence on degraded nodes. :raised_hands:
